title: Research Engine Observability, Agent Operations & Chat Bridge v1
goal: Build a low-overhead, provenance-preserving operations layer for the autonomous research engine that provides a live terminal HUD, durable per-agent telemetry and throughput metrics, empirical Codex 5-hour/weekly allowance forecasting, ChatGPT-visible status mirroring, and a safe asynchronous bridge for agents to request high-level reasoning from ChatGPT without paid API fallback or direct scientific-state mutation.
acceptance_criteria: A terminal HUD refreshes live operational state without mutating research state and shows daemon health, active run/phase, current agents/jobs, queue depth/age, source funnel, evidence/gap funnel, throughput, failures/backoffs, and Codex allowance telemetry.

Every logical agent role and ephemeral worker instance is durably identifiable, including code checkpoint, host/process generation, supported tier/model, current job, heartbeat, cumulative jobs, elapsed time, failures/retries/backoffs, and model-usage attribution.
High-frequency telemetry remains authoritative in PostgreSQL; derived rollups are reproducible from append-only or immutable event records rather than being authoritative counters only.

Per-agent, per-tier, per-model, per-job-type, and per-run usage can be queried for input, output, cached-input, reasoning-output, semantic-call count, wall time, queue time, and percentage share of total usage.

Research throughput can be reported over rolling and lifetime windows, including discovered, retained, acquired, extracted, verified, checkpointed, synthesized, gap-generated, novelty-searched, novelty-arbitrated, and human-reviewed counts plus stage latency and queue age.

The system records explicit ChatGPT/Codex plan-usage observations for both the 5-hour and weekly windows, correlates allowance deltas with durable usage events, and produces exhaustion/reset forecasts with a stated confidence level and no unsupported claim of exact token-to-plan conversion.

The initial user-observed calibration point of approximately 16% of the 5-hour allowance used during the 2026-10-01 acceptance/launch work is ingestible as a manual observation without rewriting research usage history.

A ChatGPT-readable live-ops mirror is published through GitHub without high-frequency commits to canonical code branches; ChatGPT can answer questions such as 'how is automated research going?' from that mirror plus durable rollups.

Permanent daily or run-level operational summaries preserve historical per-agent usage, throughput, backoffs, failures, and forecast observations while raw high-frequency telemetry remains in PostgreSQL.

Agents can enqueue structured Chat reasoning requests containing only bounded context/references; ChatGPT can read and respond through a durable GitHub bridge, and local agents can ingest the response without requiring an OPENAI_API_KEY.

Chat-bridge responses are advisory inputs only and cannot directly become verified scientific evidence, approve human gates, or mutate authoritative research records without the existing local validation/materialization path.

The bridge design clearly distinguishes user-triggered Chat processing from any later scheduled ChatGPT automation; no claim of autonomous real-time ChatGPT invocation is made until that path is actually validated.
Production continues to forbid paid OpenAI API fallback and secrets are never persisted in telemetry, GitHub issues, task capsules, or exported snapshots.

The observability path adds negligible research disruption: telemetry failure cannot corrupt scientific state, and publisher/HUD failure does not stop the research daemon unless an explicit safety invariant is violated.

All new schema, CLI/HUD behavior, publisher behavior, usage forecasting, agent attribution, and chat-bridge state transitions have unit/PostgreSQL integration coverage and are validated against the live sustained RF run.
Before sustained semantic work resumes, the operator can see live per-agent usage/throughput and at least a first empirical 5-hour allowance burn estimate from the HUD.

A private research-engine MCP/plugin path is evaluated as the preferred direct ChatGPT tool surface for reading ops state and submitting bounded advisory responses; plan/workspace permission limits are validated rather than assumed.

An event-driven wake-up transport is evaluated separately from the direct tool surface; Slack is the first candidate so an agent message can potentially trigger ChatGPT processing while GitHub remains the durable audit trail.
constraints: Do not stop or recreate rf-open-world-corpus-expansion-v1 merely to build observability; instrumentation must be additive/migration-safe.
Do not introduce OPENAI_API_KEY, paid OpenAI API billing, or automatic paid fallback.
Do not infer ChatGPT plan allowance from tokens alone; forecasts must be empirically calibrated against explicit observed plan-usage percentages/reset information and carry confidence/uncertainty.

Do not expose prompts, source text, secrets, credentials, or sensitive environment values in public or broad telemetry surfaces; Chat-visible payloads must be bounded operational summaries and durable record references.
Do not use workspace-control main as a high-frequency telemetry sink.
Do not create high-frequency Git commits for live telemetry; prefer a machine-maintained GitHub issue for current state and low-frequency durable rollups for history.

Do not let monitoring write to evidence_objects, verification_events, knowledge_checkpoints, synthesis_artifacts, gap_candidates, novelty_challenges, or human-review decisions except through the existing authoritative research workflows.
Do not collapse logical agent identity into PID alone; distinguish stable role identity from ephemeral process/session identity.
Do not auto-approve future scientific human-review gates.
Keep raw high-frequency operational truth local to PostgreSQL; GitHub mirrors are derived observability surfaces, not the authoritative database.
Chat reasoning requests must be idempotent, bounded, traceable to a run/job/checkpoint where applicable, and safe to ignore or retry.
Any scheduled ChatGPT bridge is limited by the product automation cadence and must be separately validated before being described as continuous agent-to-Chat communication.
Do not resume sustained semantic processing merely because the daemon architecture is proven; resume only after the HUD exposes live usage/throughput and an initial empirical allowance forecast.
Treat the current sustained RF run as durable paused work while observability is built; stopping the user systemd daemon is an operational pause, not cancellation of the run.
Do not assume a custom MCP/plugin can perform write actions on the user's current ChatGPT plan; validate the actual installed capability and permission surface before relying on it.
Do not make Slack or another message bus authoritative for research state; it may wake ChatGPT or carry bounded requests, while PostgreSQL/GitHub retain durable truth.

Implement read-only ops snapshot/report commands and a terminal HUD first, including live per-agent usage, source/evidence/gap throughput, queue/latency, failures/backoffs, and 5-hour/weekly allowance panels.

Implement explicit 5-hour/weekly Codex usage observations plus empirical forecast calibration/ETA with uncertainty and per-agent/model attribution; ingest the current ~16% 5-hour observation as the first calibration point.
Run a tightly bounded monitored calibration workload and tune model/tier/concurrency budgets before resuming sustained corpus expansion.
Implement a low-frequency Chat-visible operations mirror.
Prototype a private research-engine MCP/plugin as the preferred direct ChatGPT read/advisory-response surface; validate current-plan permissions and Secure MCP Tunnel or another private transport.
Optionally connect Slack and evaluate it as an event-driven reasoning-request wake-up bus; retain GitHub/PostgreSQL as durable truth.
Implement and validate structured Chat reasoning request/response state transitions without allowing Chat responses to bypass scientific verification or human gates.
next_safe_action: With research-engine-daemon.service confirmed inactive/dead and rf-open-world-corpus-expansion-v1 preserved, inspect the existing research_workers, research_jobs, research_job_attempts, research_usage_events, daemon health/report code, Codex execution metadata, and deployment/runtime identifiers. Write and validate the observability contract first: stable logical agent roles versus ephemeral sessions, append-only telemetry fields, derived metric formulas/windows, retention policy, allowance-observation/forecast semantics, HUD panel contract, Chat-visible summary contract, and MCP/Slack request-response safety boundary. Then implement the read-only ops snapshot and terminal HUD without resuming semantic processing.
notes: Preferred UX: a terminal HUD launched from Bash/CLI, backed by read-only PostgreSQL queries rather than Bash scraping. Proposed Chat-visible mirror: one machine-maintained GitHub issue for current state plus low-frequency permanent daily/run rollups; raw high-frequency telemetry remains PostgreSQL-authoritative. Proposed Chat bridge: agents create bounded structured reasoning requests that are mirrored to GitHub issues; ChatGPT can read/update them when invoked. This is not equivalent to a direct autonomous ChatGPT conversation API and must not be described as such until separately validated.
